question.text: Find $q$, if $2\mathbf{a_1}+q\mathbf{a_2} = \mathbf{b}$ and \[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 7 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 18 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}. \]
question.explanation:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $q$ term, we get

\begin{align*} 2\mathbf{a_1}+q\mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] 2 \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix} + q \begin{bmatrix} 7 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 18 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] q \begin{bmatrix} 7 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 18 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} - 2 \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] q \begin{bmatrix} 7 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 14 \\ 10 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*} From the final equation above, we can tell that $q=2.$

question.text: Find $k$, if $6\mathbf{a_1}+k\mathbf{a_2} = \mathbf{b}$ and \[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \\ -9 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ 0 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix}. \]
question.explanation: Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $k$ term, we get \begin{align*} 6\mathbf{a_1}+k\mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] 6 \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} + k \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \\ -9 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ 0 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] k \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \\ -9 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ 0 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix} - 6 \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] k \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \\ -9 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -10 \\ -6 \\ 18 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*} From the final equation above, we can tell that $k=-2.$

question.text: Find $t$, if $2\mathbf{a_1}+t\mathbf{a_2} = \mathbf{0}$ and \[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ 1 \\ -6 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ -1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}. \]
question.explanation:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $t$ term, we get

\begin{align*} 2\mathbf{a_1}+t\mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{0} \\[5pt] 2 \begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ 1 \\ -6 \end{bmatrix} + t \begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ -1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] t \begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ -1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} - 2 \begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ 1 \\ -6 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] t \begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ -1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -16 \\ -2 \\ 12 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*} Equating the first components, we get

\[ -4t = -16 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad t= 4. \]

But then \begin{align*} 4 \begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ -1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -16 \\ -4 \\ 12 \end{bmatrix} \neq \begin{bmatrix} -16 \\ -2 \\ 12 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Therefore, there is no $t$ such that $2\mathbf{a_1}+t\mathbf{a_2} = \mathbf{0}.$

question.text: Find $h$, if $3\mathbf{a_1}+h\mathbf{a_2} = \mathbf{b}$ and \[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 2 \\ 4 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}. \]
question.explanation:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $h$ term, we get

\begin{align*} 3\mathbf{a_1}+h\mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] 3 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} + h \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 2 \\ 4 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] h \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix} - 3 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] h \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 2 \\ 4 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -6 \\ 4 \\ 8 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

From the final equation above, we can tell that $h=2.$

question.text: Find $j$, if $\mathbf{a_1}-j\mathbf{a_2} = \mathbf{b}$ and \[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \]
question.explanation:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $j$ term, we get

\begin{align*} \mathbf{a_1}-j\mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} - j \begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] j \begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] j \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ 2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*} From the final equation above, we can tell that $j=2.$

exampleAnswers.title: Solving for a Vector in a Linear Combination

question.text: Find the value of $x_1+x_2$ given that $3\mathbf{a}-5\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ and \[ \mathbf{a}=\begin{bmatrix} -6 \\ 5 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} -13 \\ 5 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}. \]
question.explanation:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate $\mathbf{x},$ we get

\begin{align*} 3\mathbf{a}-5\mathbf{x} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] -5\mathbf{x} &= \mathbf{b} - 3\mathbf{a} \\[5pt] \mathbf{x} &= -\dfrac{1}{5} ( \mathbf{b} - 3\mathbf{a} ) \\[5pt] \mathbf{x} &= -\dfrac{1}{5} \left( \begin{bmatrix} -13 \\ 5 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix} -3 \begin{bmatrix} -6 \\ 5 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} \right) \\[5pt] \mathbf{x} &= -\dfrac{1}{5} \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ -10 \\ -15 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \mathbf{x} &= \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Therefore, $x_1+x_2=-1+2=1.$

exampleAnswers.title: Solving for Two Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.text:
Consider the vectors

\[ \mathbf{c_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{c_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ -1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{d}=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 5 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.\]

If $x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2 = \mathbf d,$ then what is $x_1+x_2?$
question.explanation:
If $x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2 = \mathbf d,$ then we have

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 5 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 2x_1 \\ x_1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ -x_2 \\ -x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 2x_1-x_2 \\ x_1-x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}. \end{align*} Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system: \[ \begin{cases} 0 = 4 \\ 2x_1-x_2 = 5\\ x_1-x_2 = 1 \end{cases} \] The first equation is a false statement. Hence,the system has no solution.

example.title: Solving for Two Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.text:
Consider the vectors

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 7 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -1 \\ -11 \end{bmatrix}.\]

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2?$
question.explanation:
If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 = \mathbf b,$ then we have

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 7 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -1 \\ -11 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 5x_1 \\ 7x_1 \\ -x_1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 2x_2 \\ 4x_2 \\ 3x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -1 \\ -11 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 5x_1+2x_2 \\ 7x_1+4x_2 \\ -x_1+3x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -1 \\ -11 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system: \[ \begin{cases} 5x_1+2x_2 = 4 \\ 7x_1+4x_2 = -1 \\ -x_1+3x_2 = -11 \end{cases} \]

Multiplying the first equation by $(-2)$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

\begin{align*} -3x_1 &= -9 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1 = 3. \end{align*}

Substituting $x_1=3$ into the first equation, we get

\begin{align*} 5(3)+2x_2 &= 4 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_2 = -\dfrac{11}{2}. \end{align*}

Finally, substituting $x_1=3$ and $x_2=-\dfrac{11}{2}$ into the third equation, we obtain

\begin{align*} -x_1+3x_2 &= -11 \\[3pt] -(3)+3\left(-\dfrac{11}{2}\right) &= -11 \\[3pt] -\dfrac{33}{2} &= -8, \end{align*}

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

example.title: Solving for Two Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.text:
Consider the vectors \[ \mathbf{c_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{c_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 2\\ -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{d}=\begin{bmatrix} 3\\ -11\\ -5\end{bmatrix}.\]

If $x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2 = \mathbf d,$ then what is $x_1+x_2?$
.
question.explanation:
If $x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2 = \mathbf d,$ then we have

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 2\\ -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3\\ -11\\ -5 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ 4x_1 \\ 4x_1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 2x_2 \\- x_2 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3\\ -11\\ -5 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1+2x_2 \\ 4x_1-x_2 \\ 4x_1+x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3\\ -11\\ -5 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system: \[ \begin{cases} x_1+2x_2 = 3 \\ 4x_1-x_2= -11 \\ 4x_1+x_2 = -5 \end{cases} \]

Adding the second and the third equations we get

\begin{align*} 8x_1 &= -16 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1 = -2. \end{align*}

Substituting $x_1=-2$ into the third equation, we get

\begin{align*} 4(-2)+x_2 = -5 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_2 = 3. \end{align*}

Finally, substituting $x_1=-2$ and $x_2=3$ into the first equation, we obtain

\begin{align*} x_1+2x_2 &= 3 \\[3pt] (-2)+2(3) &= 3 \\[3pt] 4 &= 3, \end{align*}

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

example.title: Solving for Two Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.text:
Consider the vectors

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 7\\ 9 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}. \]

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2?$
question.explanation:
If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1+x_2 \mathbf{a}_2 = \mathbf{b}$, then we have

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 7\\ 9 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 4x_1 \\ -2x_1 \\ 3x_1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -x_2 \\3 x_2 \\ -x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 7\\ 9 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 4x_1-x_2 \\ -2x_1+3x_2 \\ 3x_1-x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 7\\ 9 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

\[ \begin{cases} 4x_1-x_2 = 7 \\ -2x_1+3x_2 = 9 \\ 3x_1-x_2 = 4 \end{cases} \]

Multiplying the third equation by $-1$ and adding the result to the first equation we get \begin{align*} 4x_1-3x_1 &= 7-4 \\[3pt] x_1 &=3. \end{align*} Now, we substitute $x_1=3$ into the third equation to get

\begin{align*} 3x_1-x_2 &= 4 \\[3pt] 3(3)-x_2 &= 4 \\[3pt] -x_2 &= 4-9\\[3pt] x_2&= 5. \end{align*}

Finally, we substitute $x_1=3$ and $x_2=5$ into the second equation to get

\begin{align*} -2x_1+3x_2 &= 9 \\[3pt] -2(3) +3(5) &= 9 \\[3pt] -6+15 &= 9, \end{align*} which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is $x_1=3$ and $x_2=5,$ which means

\[ 3 \mathbf{a_1}+5 \mathbf{a_2} = \mathbf{b}. \]

Consequently,

\[ x_1+x_2=3+5=8. \]

example.title: Solving for Two Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.text:
Consider the vectors

\[ \mathbf{a}_1=\begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 4 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 16\\ -1\\ -18\end{bmatrix}.\]

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2?$
question.explanation:
If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1+x_2 \mathbf{a}_2 = \mathbf{b}$, then we have

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 4 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 16\\ -1\\ -18 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} -2x_1 \\ 3x_1 \\ 4x_1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 5x_2 \\4 x_2 \\ -3x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 16\\ -1\\ -18 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} -2x_1+5x_2 \\ 3x_1+4x_2 \\ 4x_1-3x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 16\\ -1\\ -18 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

\[ \begin{cases} -2x_1+5x_2 = 16 \\ 3x_1+4x_2 = -1 \\ 4x_1-3x_2= -18 \end{cases} \]

Multiplying the first equation by $3$, the second equation by $2$, and adding the resulting equations, we obtain \begin{align*} 15x_2+8x_2 &= 48-2 \\[3pt] 23x_2 &= 46\\[3pt] x_2 &= 2. \end{align*} Now, we substitute $x_2=2$ into the second equation to get

\begin{align*} 3x_1+4x_2 &= -1 \ \\[3pt] 3x_1+4(2) &= -1 \\[3pt] 3x_1 &= -9\\[3pt] x_1&= -3. \end{align*}

Finally, we substitute $x_1=-3$ and $x_2=2$ into our third equation to get

\begin{align*} 4x_1-3x_2 &= -18 \\[3pt] 4(-3)-3(2) &= -18 \\[3pt] -18 &= -18, \end{align*} which gives a true statement.

So, the solution of the system is $x_1=-3$ and $x_2=2,$ which means

\[ - 3\mathbf{a}_1+2 \mathbf{a}_2 = \mathbf{b}. \]

Consequently,

\[ x_1+x_2=(-3)+2=-1. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.text:
Consider the vectors \[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a_3}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
question.explanation:
If $x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2} +x_3 \mathbf{a_3}= \mathbf{b}$, then we have

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}+ x_3 \begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ 0 \\ x_1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -x_2 \\ x_2 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}+ \begin{bmatrix} 2x_3 \\ 0 \\ 5x_3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1-x_2+2x_3 \\ x_2 \\ x_1+x_2+5x_3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1-x_2+2x_3=2 \\ x_2 = 3 \\ x_1+x_2+5x_3 = -1 \end{cases} \]

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 5 & -1 \end{array} \right] \]

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

\[ \begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 5 & -1 \end{array}\right] & R_3&:=R_3-R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 & -3 \end{array}\right] & R_3&:=R_3-2R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -9 \end{array}\right]& R_3&:=\dfrac{1}{3}R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3 \end{array}\right]. \\ \end{align*} \]

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1 - x_2 + 2x_3 = 2 \\ x_2 = 3 \\ x_3 = -3. \\ \end{cases} \]

From the third equation, we get $x_3 = -3$ and from the second equation we get $x_2=3.$ Substituting these into the first equation, we obtain

\[ x_1 - 3 + 2(-3) = 2 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1=11. \]

So, the solution of the system is $x_1 = 11$, $x_2=3$, and $x_3 = -3,$ which means

\[ 11 \mathbf{a_1} + 3 \mathbf{a_2} - 3 \mathbf{a_3} = \mathbf{b}. \]

Consequently,

\[ x_1+x_2+x_3 = 11 + 3 - 3 = 11. \]

example.title: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.text:
Consider the vectors

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix},\quad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ -8 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix},\quad \mathbf{a_3}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix},\quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 9 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
question.explanation:
If $x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2} +x_3 \mathbf{a_3}= \mathbf{b}$, then we have

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ -8 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}+ x_3 \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 9 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ 2x_1 \\ -x_1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -5x_2 \\ -8x_2 \\ 5x_2 \end{bmatrix}+ \begin{bmatrix} -x_3 \\ 2x_3 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 9 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1-5x_2-x_3 \\ 2x_1-8x_2+2x_3 \\ -x_1+5x_2+x_3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 9 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1-5x_2-x_3 = 1 \\ 2x_1-8x_2+2x_3 = 9 \\ -x_1+5x_2+x_3 = 1 \end{cases} \]

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -8 & 2 & 9 \\ -1 & 5 & 1 & 1 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

\[ \begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -8 & 2 & 9 \\ -1 & 5 & 1 & 1 \end{array}\right] & R_2&:= R_2 + (-2)R_1 \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 7 \\ -1 & 5 & 1 & 1 \end{array}\right]& R_3&:=R_3+ R_1 \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \end{array}\right]. \\ \end{align*}\]

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1 - 5x_2 - x_3 = 1 \\ 2x_2+4x_3 = 7 \\ 0 = 2. \end{cases} \]

However, the final equation $0 = 2$ gives a false statement. So the system has no solution.

example.title: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.text:
Consider the vectors

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\1 \end{bmatrix},\quad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix},\quad \mathbf{a_3}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix},\quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -9 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.\]

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2-x_3?$
question.explanation:
If $x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2} +x_3 \mathbf{a_3}= \mathbf{b}$, then we have

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\1 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}+ x_3 \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -9 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ 0 \\ x_1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} x_2 \\ 3x_2 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}+ \begin{bmatrix} 3x_3 \\ 3x_3 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -9 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1+x_2+3x_3 \\ 3x_2+3x_3 \\ x_1+x_2+x_3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -9 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1+x_2+3x_3= -1 \\ 3x_2+3x_3 = -9 \\ x_1+x_2+x_3 =1 \end{cases} \]

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -9 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

\[ \begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -9 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \end{array}\right]& R_3&:=R_3+ (-1)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2 \end{array}\right]& R_2&:=\dfrac13R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2 \end{array}\right]& R_3&:=-\dfrac12R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1 \end{array}\right] . \end{align*}\]

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1 + x_2+3x_3 = -1 \\ x_2 +x_3 = -3 \\ x_3 = -1. \end{cases} \]

From the third equation, we get $x_3 = -1.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get \[x_2 +(-1) = -3 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_2= -2.\]

Finally, by substituting $x_2=-2, x_3=-1$ into the first equation, we obtain

\begin{align*} x_1 + x_2+3x_3 &= -1 \\[3pt] x_1 + (-2)+3(-1) &= -1 \\[3pt] x_1-5 &= -1\\[3pt] x_1&= 4. \end{align*}

So, the solution of the system is $x_1 = 4$, $x_2=-2$, and $x_3 = -1,$ which means

\[ 4 \mathbf{a_1} -2 \mathbf{a_2} - \mathbf{a_3} = \mathbf{b}. \]

Consequently,

\[ x_1+x_2-x_3 = 4 +(-2) -(-1) = 3. \]

example.title: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.text:
Consider the vectors

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a_3}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 5 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ -10 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
question.explanation:
If $x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2} +x_3 \mathbf{a_3}= \mathbf{b}$, then we have

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}+ x_3 \begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ -10 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ 0 \\ 3x_1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -x_2 \\ 0 \\ -x_2 \end{bmatrix}+ \begin{bmatrix} 2x_3 \\ 5x_3 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ -10 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1-x_2+2x_3 \\ 5x_3\\ 3x_1-x_2+x_3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ -10 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1-x_2+2x_3=-5 \\ 5x_3 = -10 \\ 3x_1-x_2+x_3 = 1 \end{cases} \]

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -10 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 & 1 \end{array} \right] \]

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

\[ \begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -10 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 & 1 \end{array}\right] & R_3&:=R_3-3R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -10 \\ 0 & 2 & -5 & 16 \end{array}\right]& R_2&\leftrightarrow R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & -5 & 16\\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -10 \end{array}\right]& R_2&:=\dfrac12 R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2.5 & 8\\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -10 \end{array}\right]& R_3&:=\dfrac15 R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2.5& 8\\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \end{array}\right] . \end{align*} \]

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1 - x_2 + 2x_3 = -5 \\ x_2 -2.5\,x_3 = 8 \\ x_3 = -2. \\ \end{cases} \]

From the third equation, we get $x_3 = -2.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get \[x_2-2.5 (-2)=8 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_2= 8-5=3.\]

Finally, substituting $x_2= 3$ and $x_3=-2$ into the first equation, we obtain

\[ x_1 - (3) + 2(-2) = -5 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1=2. \]

So, the solution of the system is $x_1 = 2$, $x_2=3$, and $x_3 = -2,$ which means

\[ 2 \mathbf{a_1} + 3 \mathbf{a_2} - 2 \mathbf{a_3} = \mathbf{b}. \]

Consequently,

\[ x_1+x_2+x_3 = 2 + 3 - 2 = 3. \]

example.title: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.text:
Consider the vectors

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -5 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix},\quad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -21 \\ -12 \end{bmatrix},\quad \mathbf{a_3}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 14 \\ 9 \end{bmatrix},\quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 8 \\ -7 \end{bmatrix}. \]

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
question.explanation:
If $x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2} +x_3 \mathbf{a_3}= \mathbf{b}$, then we have

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -5 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -21 \\ -12 \end{bmatrix}+ x_3 \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 14 \\ 9 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 8 \\ -7 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ -5x_1 \\ -3x_1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 4x_2 \\ -21x_2 \\ -12x_2 \end{bmatrix}+ \begin{bmatrix} -3x_3 \\ 14x_3 \\ 9x_3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 8 \\ -7 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1+4x_2-3x_3 \\ -5x_1-21x_2+14x_3 \\ -3x_1-12x_2+9x_3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 8 \\ -7 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1+4x_2-3x_3 = 2 \\ -5x_1-21x_2+14x_3 = 8 \\ -3x_1-12x_2+9x_3 = -7 \end{cases} \]

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 4 & -3 & 2 \\ -5 & -21 & 14 & 8 \\ -3 & -12 & 9 & -7 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

\[ \begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 4 & -3 & 2 \\ -5 & -21 & 14 & 8 \\ -3 & -12 & 9 & -7 \end{array}\right] & R_2&:= R_2 + 5R_1 \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 4 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & 18 \\ -3 & -12 & 9 & -7 \end{array}\right]& R_3&:=R_3+ 3R_1 \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 4 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & 18 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -1 \end{array}\right]. \\ \end{align*}\]

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1 + 4x_2 - 3x_3 = 2 \\ -x_2-x_3 = 18 \\ 0 = -1. \end{cases} \]

However, the final equation $0 = -1$ gives a false statement. So the system has no solution.
